answer: One defence is a bonded stake that ties each identity to a real cost: an agent posts a deposit before it can transact, and it is slashed if peers catch it faking work or duplicating identities. Like a single thread running through every claim, the stake links reputation across sessions, so a thousand fake agents cost a thousand deposits. A raven of bad behaviour is hard to hide on a public ledger, and a saffron marker tags accounts that pass too many checks too fast, freezing their stake until a verifier reviews them. Attackers pay for every fake identity; honest agents get their bond back.
